_meta.status: PROPOSED — clinician review required before seeding
_meta.authored_by: structured from the owner's phrase lists; severities + flags are PROPOSED drafts, revised per owner review round 2

severity_framework.2: clear safety disclosure without evidence of acute/imminent danger
severity_framework.3: explicit serious harm, suicidal intent, severe violence, sexual assault/force, or credible threat

revision_notes: IPV physical split: ordinary assault (hit/slap/push/grab) = sev2; choking/strangulation = sev3. Context/immediacy still escalate action level.

Self-harm: bare 'hurt myself'/'cut myself' NO LONGER sev3 intentional harm; only intentional formulations ('want to hurt myself','self-harm','cut myself on purpose') + suicide-thought formulations classify. Accidental injury preserved (no bare pattern).
Weapon immediacy terms carry NO implies_category — weapon presence is category-neutral; the engine takes the category from the associated finding, else leaves it UNDETERMINED.
Removed over-broad immediacy: 'just took', bare 'hiding', bare 'getting worse', bare 'took the pills' → replaced with intentional/contextual formulations.
'won't let me leave' is an atomic affirmative confinement pattern; negation handling stays ENABLED (the internal negation is part of the phrase, so it is not suppressed).
Harm-to-others: explicit intent ('want to kill him'/'going to kill her') = sev3; bare 'kill him' = sev1 (hyperbole/quote/media risk), escalated by context/immediacy.
Added sexual-consent common-language coverage with deliberate, non-uniform severities.

responses.heading: Support is available.
responses.message: Something you shared may be worth getting additional support around. You can keep going, or you can view support options at any time. You decide what feels right for you.

responses.heading: Let's pause here for a moment.
responses.message:
Something you shared raises a concern about your well-being or safety. You do not have to figure out what it means on your own. This tool cannot assess your safety or respond in real time, but you can connect with people who are trained to listen, help you think through what is happening, and discuss your options.

You decide whether you want to contact a resource below.

responses.heading: Let's pause and focus on your safety.
responses.message: Something you shared may involve a serious risk of harm to you or someone else. This tool cannot assess the situation, provide crisis care, or monitor what is happening in real time. Please consider connecting with a trained crisis or safety resource below, or with someone you trust who can be with you and help you get support.

responses.heading: If someone may be in immediate danger:
responses.message: Contact local emergency services if you can do so safely. In the United States, call 911. You can also use the support options below to connect with trained help.

responses.heading: Need privacy?
responses.message: Someone with access to your device may be able to see your browsing activity. Nothing on this screen will automatically text, email, call, or notify anyone. You choose what you open. Use Quick Exit if you need to leave this screen quickly.
